West Indies still had Justin Greaves and Kevin Sinclair out in the middle when the last session started but added just a few runs and ran out of tail. Australia are in the driving seat at the moment. They need 216 runs to win. The hosts are the favourites but the ball is doing enough for West Indies to inspire and end the day on a high. Can they scalp some wickets in this small phase? Let's find out.

The pain is too much for Shamar Joseph to bear and that will be the end of the Windies innings. A horrible hour with the bat for West Indies and on top of that Shamar Joseph is injured now. They were at one stage cruising through and in full control of this match but Australia turned the tables. West Indies lost half of their side inside 50 runs.The momentum changing period was when Kavem Hodge got out and all thanks to Travis Head at short leg for his quick reflexes.

Hello and welcome to the action of Day 3 between Australia and West Indies. The match is wonderfully poised right now. We feel whoever dominates the day has the best chance to win the game. Australia declared their innings after coming out of a dreadful phase. They lost four wickets for not many runs but the stand between Khawaja and Carey and later, Cummins fifty got them close to the Windies score. The visitors lost Chanderpaul right at the end of Day 2. Australia will be fresh and all set to get through the Windies batting order who’ll hope to bat atleast for a day. Stay tuned.
...Day 3, Session 1...

Right then, that is it from an exciting Day 2 of this Day/Night Test. The game is nicely poised at the moment as we head to the 'Moving Day' where the Aussies will look to make early inroads to restrict the visitors to post a big target while West Indies will be hoping to do the exact opposite by building up partnerships in the middle. Day 3 will start on 27th January, Saturday at 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT), but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

Pat Cummins joined Usman Khawaja in the middle for the last session when the Aussies were more than 100 runs behind. Both of them looked solid out there and slowly built up a partnership and at a good rate as well. The Aussie skipper was peppered with short balls, but he managed to stick around while scoring runs as well. He got settled and started to find the boundaries along with Khawaja, and they added 81 runs together to get them closer to the total. Even though Khawaja ended up as the first Test victim of Kevin Sinclair which brought out the backflip celebration, Cummins continued to attack the bowlers. He registered his third Test fifty and first as a skipper and remained unbeaten on 64 which is his highest individual score in this format. The hosts declared with one wicket in hand and 22 runs behind to have a go at the West Indies batters under light. Mitchell Starc created an opportunity but Steven Smith spilled it to get rid of Kraigg Brathwaite which you do not see very often. It looked like the Windies openers would see out till the end, but Josh Hazlewood had different ideas and dismissed Tagenarine Chanderpaul in the last over before Stumps which gives the Aussies momentum going into the 'Moving Day'.

In the second session, Mitchell Marsh played a few lusty blows at the start but couldn't handle the pace and bounce of Alzarri Joseph and got out. However, then the fightback started from the Aussies just like their opponents at the same stage on Day 1. Alex Carey got a bit fortunate when he was on 8 as the ball but the bails remained on the stumps and he survived. He made full use of that and smashed his fastest Test fifty to release the pressure of them. Usman Khawaja was solid as usual on the other end and they added 96 runs together before Carey holed out to Shamar Joseph. Just before going into the Tea break, Joseph removed Mitchell Starc with the Aussies still well behind in the game.

West Indies started Day 2 very positively with Kevin Sinclair and Kemar Roach showing good intent. The former was the aggressor and notched up a Test fifty on debut but got out soon after but his knock helped the Windies go past the 300-run mark. However, they were absolutely brilliant with the ball right from the start. Roach dismissed Steven Smith in the very first over while Alzarri Joseph got rid of Marnus Labuschagne in the second. Just before Dinner, Roach then got two in two balls to send Cameron Green and Travis Head packing as the Windies ended that session on top.

Australia end Day 2 with a crucial wicket! We have had six sessions in this Test and in five of them, a wicket has fallen in the last over. It was another day where both teams went hard at each other and pushed their opponents to the limit. At this point in time, West Indies lead by 35 runs with nine wickets still in hand and a lot of time in this Test remaining. We saw excellent spells from Kemar Roach and Alzarri Joseph while Usman Khawaja solidly anchored the innings for the Aussies. Alex Carey and Pat Cummins entertained us with their attacking knocks as well, and the crowd at Gabba surely got their worth for money.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Josh Hazlewood has finally rewarded himself with a wicket! Pat Cummins' plan working to perfection! Josh Hazlewood charges in and delivers it on a good length outside off. Tagenarine Chanderpaul unlike him, opts to reach for it but the ball swings away from him. Alex Carey is confident and he brings out a loud appeal.
